mock_data.title: Coping with Misery
mock_data.passage:
Jane was feeling extremely miserable. Just a few months ago she had been happily looking forward to her wedding day, but three weeks ago she had received a letter out of the blue from her fiancé, Peter. The letter said that he wanted to break off their engagement because he had fallen in love with someone else.

Jane was devastated. She was extremely fortunate in having several very loyal and supportive friends and they provided a shoulder to cry on. However, as time went on and Jane still could not stop crying and could not stop talking about how her life was ruined, her friends gradually became impatient with her. One by one, in their different ways, they tried to get her to put the past behind her.

Lucy was quite gentle with Jane and pointed out to her that she would not always feel so bad about her broken engagement as she did just then. 'Time is a great healer', she said. 'Obviously, you'll never forget what's happened, but the pain will get less.' Jane was not convinced and went on weeping.

Mary was anxious to make Jane see that the broken engagement was not her fault, but that it was not Peter's fault either. 'These things happen', she said in what she hoped was a comforting manner. Jane, alas, was in no fit state to be comforted. By this time, she was suffering from depression and was seeing a professional counsellor. She had stopped attending her college classes and hardly ever left her house.

Judy, not realizing that Jane was actually ill, tried a more brutal approach than the rest of her friends. 'You're just going to have to pull yourself together,' she said. 'What's done is done and there's no use in crying over spilt milk. Peter's not coming back and you must face facts. You'll just have to get on with your life. It is time to move on. If you don't get your act together and start going to college, you'll have to repeat the year.' People who are suffering from depression have very little energy and Judy's boisterous approach to her problems had little effect on Jane, except that she took to avoiding her as much as possible.

The person who had given the best advice was Lucy. In time, Jane did begin to feel better, but her recovery was slow.
mock_data.passageB1:
Jane was very sad. A few months ago, she was happy and excited about her wedding. But three weeks ago, she got a letter from her fiancé, Peter. The letter said he wanted to end their engagement because he was in love with someone else.

Jane was very upset. She was lucky to have good friends who supported her. They let her cry and listened to her problems. But after some time, Jane’s friends started to get tired of her sadness. They tried to help her forget the past.

Lucy was kind to Jane. She told her that she would not always feel so bad. Lucy said, 'Time helps you feel better. You will not forget, but the pain will decrease.' Jane did not believe her and kept crying.

Mary wanted Jane to know that the broken engagement was not her fault, or Peter’s fault. She tried to comfort her by saying, 'These things happen.' But Jane was too sad to be comforted. She was depressed and seeing a doctor. She stopped going to her college classes and stayed at home.

Judy did not know that Jane was ill. She tried to be tough with Jane. She said, 'You need to try harder. What's done is done, and you can’t change it. Peter is not coming back, and you must accept it. You need to continue with your life. It's time to move on. If you don't go to college, you will have to repeat the year.' Jane did not have much energy because she was depressed. Judy’s strong words did not help, and Jane started to avoid her.

Lucy gave the best advice. After some time, Jane started to feel better. But it took a long time for her to recover.
mock_data.passageB2:
Jane was feeling utterly despondent. Only a few months earlier, she had been eagerly anticipating her wedding, but just three weeks ago, she received a shocking letter from her fiancé, Peter. He wrote that he was calling off their engagement because he had fallen for someone else.

Jane was completely heartbroken. Fortunately, she had several incredibly loyal and supportive friends who offered a shoulder to cry on. However, as time passed and Jane continued to be consumed by her grief and constantly talked about how her life was ruined, her friends gradually began to lose patience. In their own ways, they each tried to encourage her to move on from the past.

Lucy was quite gentle with Jane, reminding her that she wouldn't always feel as devastated as she did in that moment. 'Time is a great healer,' she said. 'Of course, you'll never completely forget what happened, but the pain will subside.' Jane remained unconvinced and continued to weep.

Mary was eager to help Jane understand that the broken engagement wasn't her fault, nor was it entirely Peter's. 'These things happen,' she said, hoping to offer some comfort. Sadly, Jane was in no state to be comforted. By this point, she was experiencing depression and was consulting a professional therapist. She had stopped attending her college classes and rarely left the house, becoming increasingly isolated.

Judy, unaware that Jane was genuinely unwell, adopted a more blunt approach than the others. 'You just need to get a grip,' she said. 'What's done is done, and there's no point in dwelling on it. Peter isn't coming back, and you have to accept the reality. You need to get on with your life. It's time to look ahead. If you don't pull yourself together and start going to college, you'll have to repeat the year.' People suffering from depression often lack motivation, and Judy's forceful approach had little impact on Jane, except that she began avoiding her whenever possible. Judy's words fell on deaf ears.

Ultimately, Lucy's advice proved to be the most helpful. Over time, Jane did begin to feel better, but her recovery was a slow and arduous process, and she had to seek professional help to get back on her feet.
mock_data.passageC1:
Jane found herself in the throes of profound misery. Mere months prior, she had been buoyantly anticipating her wedding, a future now irrevocably shattered. A mere three weeks earlier, a letter had arrived, seemingly out of nowhere, from Peter, her fiancé. In it, he declared his intention to call off their engagement, confessing he had succumbed to the allure of another.

The impact on Jane was, predictably, devastating. Fortunately, she was blessed with a coterie of devoted and supportive friends, individuals who readily offered a sympathetic ear. However, as the weeks wore on, and Jane remained mired in her grief, unable to stem the tide of tears or cease lamenting the perceived ruination of her life, her friends' patience began to wear thin. Each, in their own distinct way, attempted to encourage her to relegate the past to its rightful place.

Lucy, employing a gentler approach, attempted to reassure Jane that the acute pain of the broken engagement would, in time, abate. 'Time is, indeed, a great healer,' she asserted. 'While the memory will undoubtedly endure, its sting will inevitably lessen.' Jane, however, remained unconvinced, her weeping unabated.

Mary, driven by a desire to absolve Jane of any perceived culpability, equally sought to exonerate Peter. 'These things, regrettably, do occur,' she offered, aiming for a tone of solace. Sadly, Jane was in no state to derive comfort from such platitudes. By this juncture, she had succumbed to depression, seeking counsel from a qualified professional. She had ceased attending her college lectures and had become virtually housebound.

Judy, perhaps failing to fully appreciate the clinical nature of Jane's condition, adopted a considerably more forceful strategy than her counterparts. 'You simply must muster the strength to pull yourself together,' she declared. 'What has transpired is irreversible, and there is no point in dwelling on what cannot be altered. Peter is not returning, and you must confront this reality. It is imperative that you move forward with your life. The time has come to regain control of your affairs and resume your studies, or you risk academic failure.' However, those afflicted with depression characteristically experience a profound lack of energy, and Judy's robust approach proved largely ineffective, save for prompting Jane to avoid her company whenever possible.

In retrospect, it was Lucy's counsel that proved most efficacious. Over time, Jane did, in fact, begin to experience a gradual amelioration of her condition, although her recovery remained a protracted process, a testament to the enduring nature of emotional wounds.

mock_data.translation:
Jeyn juda baxtsiz his qilardi. Bir necha oy oldin u to'y kunini intiqlik bilan kutayotgan edi, ammo uch hafta oldin u o'zining nishonlisi Piterdan kutilmagan xat oldi. Xatda u kimdir boshqasini sevib qolgan va shuning uchun ularning nikohini bekor qilmoqchi ekani aytilgan edi.

Jeyn vayron bo'ldi. U bir nechta juda sodiq va qo'llab-quvvatlovchi do'stlarga ega edi va ular unga yig'lash uchun yelka taqdim etdilar. Biroq, vaqt o'tib, Jeyn hali ham yig'lashni to'xtata olmadi va hayoti barbod bo'lganligi haqida gapirishni to'xtata olmadi, do'stlari asta-sekin unga sabrsiz bo'la boshladilar. Bir-birlari ortidan, har xil yo'llar bilan, ular uni o'tmishni ortda qoldirishga harakat qildilar.

Lyusi Jeyn bilan juda yumshoq muomala qildi va unga hozir his qilayotganidek, buzilgan nikoh haqida doimo yomon his qilmasligini tushuntirdi. "Vaqt eng yaxshi shifokor", dedi u. "Albatta, nima bo'lganini hech qachon unutmaysiz, ammo og'riq kamayadi." Jeyn ishonmadi va yig'lashda davom etdi.

Meri Jeynni buzilgan nikoh uning aybi emasligini, ammo bu Piterning ham aybi emasligini tushunishga intildi. "Bunday narsalar bo'ladi", dedi u tasalli beruvchi ohangda. Jeyn, afsuski, tasalli olish uchun yaroqsiz holatda edi. Bu vaqtga kelib, u depressiyadan aziyat chekardi va professional maslahatchi bilan uchrashardi. U kollejdagi darslariga qatnashishni to'xtatdi va uyidan deyarli hech qachon chiqmasdi.

Judi, Jeyn aslida kasal ekanligini tushunmay, do'stlarining qolganlariga qaraganda ko'proq qattiq yondashuvni sinab ko'rdi. "Sen shunchaki o'zingni to'plamoging kerak", dedi u. "Qilingan ish qilingan va to'kilgan sutga yig'lashdan foyda yo'q. Piter qaytib kelmaydi va sen haqiqatga yuzlanishing kerak. Sen shunchaki hayotingni davom ettirishga majbur bo'lasan. Oldinga siljish vaqti keldi. Agar sen o'zingni to'plamasing va kollejga bormang boshlamaying, yilni takrorlashing kerak bo'ladi." Depressiyadan aziyat chekayotgan odamlar juda kam energiyaga ega va Judining shiddatli yondashuvining uning muammolariga kam ta'siri bo'ldi, faqat Jeyn uni iloji boricha chetlab o'tishga harakat qila boshladi.

Eng yaxshi maslahat bergan odam Lyusi edi. Vaqt o'tib, Jeyn o'zini yaxshiroq his qila boshladi, ammo uning tiklanishi sekin edi.

Jeyn juda xafa edi. Bir necha oy oldin u baxtli va to'yi haqida hayajonda edi. Ammo uch hafta oldin u kuyovi Piterdan xat oldi. Xatda u boshqa birovni sevib qolgani uchun unashtiruvni tugatmoqchi ekanligini aytgan edi.

Jeyn juda xafa bo'ldi. Uning uni qo'llab-quvvatlagan yaxshi do'stlari borligi unga omad keltirdi. Ular unga yig'lashga ruxsat berishdi va uning muammolarini tinglashdi. Ammo biroz vaqt o'tgach, Jeynning do'stlari uning qayg'usidan charchashni boshladilar. Ular unga o'tmishni unutishga yordam berishga harakat qilishdi.

Lyusi Jeynga mehribon edi. U unga doim ham o'zini bunchalik yomon his qilmasligini aytdi. Lyusi: "Vaqt o'zingizni yaxshi his qilishga yordam beradi. Siz unutmaysiz, lekin og'riq kamayadi", dedi. Jeyn unga ishonmadi va yig'lashda davom etdi.

Meri Jeynga unashtiruvning buzilishi uning aybi emasligini yoki Piterning aybi emasligini tushuntirmoqchi edi. U unga "Bunday narsalar bo'lib turadi" deb aytib, uni yupatishga harakat qildi. Ammo Jeyn yupatilish uchun juda xafa edi. U tushkunlikka tushgan edi va shifokorga ko'rinayotgan edi. U kollej darslariga borishni to'xtatdi va uyda qoldi.

Judi Jeynning kasal ekanligini bilmas edi. U Jeyn bilan qattiqqo'l bo'lishga harakat qildi. U: "Siz ko'proq harakat qilishingiz kerak. Bo'lgan ish bo'ldi va siz uni o'zgartira olmaysiz. Piter qaytib kelmaydi va siz buni qabul qilishingiz kerak. Siz hayotingizni davom ettirishingiz kerak. Oldinga yurish vaqti keldi. Agar kollejga bormasangiz, yilni qayta o'qishingizga to'g'ri keladi", dedi. Jeyn tushkunlikka tushgani uchun unchalik kuchga ega emas edi. Judining qattiq so'zlari yordam bermadi va Jeyn undan qochishni boshladi.

Lyusi eng yaxshi maslahatni berdi. Biroz vaqt o'tgach, Jeyn o'zini yaxshi his qila boshladi. Ammo uning sog'ayishi uchun ko'p vaqt kerak bo'ldi.

Jeyn o'zini butunlay tushkun his qilardi. Bir necha oy oldin u to'yi bo'lishini intiqlik bilan kutayotgan edi, ammo bundan atigi uch hafta oldin unga kuyovi Piterdan hayratlanarli xat keldi. U boshqa birovga ko'ngil qo'ygani sababli unashtiruvni bekor qilayotganini yozgan edi.

Jeyn butunlay qalbini yo'qotgan edi. Yaxshiyamki, uning juda sadoqatli va qo'llab-quvvatlovchi bir nechta do'stlari bor edi, ular yig'lash uchun yelka tutdilar. Biroq, vaqt o'tishi bilan Jeyn qayg'usi bilan band bo'lib, hayoti buzilgani haqida doimiy ravishda gapiravergach, do'stlari asta-sekin sabr-toqatini yo'qota boshladilar. Ular har biri o'zicha uni o'tmishdan o'tib ketishga undashga harakat qilishdi.

Lyusi Jeyn bilan ancha muloyim muomala qildi va unga doim ham o'sha paytdagidek xarob ahvolda bo'lmasligini eslatdi. "Vaqt - buyuk tabib", dedi u. "Albatta, nima bo'lganini hech qachon butunlay unutmayasan, lekin og'riq pasayadi." Jeyn ishonmadi va yig'lashda davom etdi.

Meri Jeynga unashtiruvning buzilishi uning aybi emasligini, Piterning ham butunlay aybi emasligini tushunishga yordam berishga intildi. "Bunday narsalar bo'lib turadi", dedi u, biroz taskin berishga umid qilib. Afsuski, Jeyn taskin topadigan ahvolda emas edi. Ayni paytda u depressiyaga tushgan va professional terapevt bilan maslahatlashayotgan edi. U kollej darslariga qatnashni to'xtatdi va uydan kamdan-kam chiqib, tobora ajralib qoldi.

Judi, Jeynning chinakam kasal ekanligini bilmagan holda, boshqalarga qaraganda ko'proq qo'pol yondashuvni qo'lladi. "O'zingni qo'lga olishing kerak", dedi u. "Nima bo'lsa bo'ldi va bunga achinib o'tirishning foydasi yo'q. Piter qaytib kelmaydi va sen haqiqatni qabul qilishing kerak. Hayotingni davom ettirishing kerak. Oldinga qarash vaqti keldi. Agar o'zingni qo'lga olmasang va kollejga bora boshlamasang, yilni qayta o'qishingga to'g'ri keladi." Depressiyadan aziyat chekayotgan odamlarda ko'pincha motivatsiya yetishmaydi va Judining qat'iy yondashuvi Jeynga deyarli ta'sir qilmadi, faqat u iloji boricha undan qochishni boshladi. Judining so'zlari qulog'iga kirmadi.

Oxir-oqibat, Lyusining maslahati eng foydali bo'ldi. Vaqt o'tishi bilan Jeyn o'zini yaxshi his qila boshladi, lekin uning tiklanishi sekin va mashaqqatli jarayon bo'ldi va u oyoqqa turish uchun professional yordamga murojaat qilishga majbur bo'ldi.

Jeyn oʻzini chuqur qaygʻu girdobida topdi. Bir necha oy oldin u toʻyidan shodiyona bilan umidvor edi, endi esa bu kelajak butunlay barbod boʻlgandi. Atigi uch hafta oldin unga Peter, uning kuyovidan kutilmaganda xat keldi. Unda u unashtiruvni bekor qilish niyatida ekanligini eʼlon qildi va boshqa birining jozibasiga berilib qolganini tan oldi.

Jeyn uchun bu taʼsir, taxmin qilinganidek, halokatli boʻldi. Yaxshiyamki, uning sodiq va qoʻllab-quvvatlovchi doʻstlari bor edi, ular har doim hamdardlik koʻrsatishga tayyor edilar. Biroq, haftalar oʻtishi bilan, Jeyn oʻz qaygʻusiga botib, koʻz yoshlarini toʻxtata olmadi yoki hayotining barbod boʻlgani haqida nolishni bas qila olmadi, doʻstlarining sabr-toqati tugay boshladi. Ularning har biri oʻziga xos tarzda uni oʻtmishni oʻz oʻrniga qoʻyishga undashga harakat qildi.

Lyusi, yumshoqroq yondashuvdan foydalanib, Jeynni unashtiruvning oʻtkir ogʻrigʻi vaqt oʻtishi bilan kamayishiga ishontirishga harakat qildi. "Vaqt, haqiqatan ham, buyuk tabib", dedi u. "Xotira, shubhasiz, saqlanib qoladi, lekin uning achchigʻi muqarrar ravishda kamayadi." Jeyn esa ishonmadi, uning yigʻlashi toʻxtamadi.

Meri, Jeynni har qanday aybdorlikdan ozod qilish istagi bilan Peterning ham aybsizligini isbotlashga harakat qildi. "Bunday narsalar, afsuski, sodir boʻladi", dedi u taskin berish ohangida. Afsuski, Jeyn bunday bemaʼni gaplardan tasalli topadigan ahvolda emas edi. Shu paytga kelib, u depressiyaga tushib, malakali mutaxassisdan maslahat soʻradi. U kollej maʼruzalariga qatnashishni toʻxtatdi va deyarli uydan chiqmaydigan boʻlib qoldi.

Jyudi, ehtimol, Jeynning ahvolining klinik tabiatini toʻliq anglamay, oʻz hamkasblariga qaraganda ancha qatʼiy strategiyani qabul qildi. "Sen shunchaki oʻzingni qoʻlga olish uchun kuch topishing kerak", dedi u. "Sodir boʻlgan narsa qaytarilmasdir va oʻzgartirib boʻlmaydigan narsaga eʼtibor qaratishning maʼnosi yoʻq. Peter qaytib kelmaydi va sen bu haqiqatga duch kelishing kerak. Hayotingni davom ettirishing shart. Ishlaringni nazoratga olish va oʻqishingni davom ettirish vaqti keldi, aks holda akademik muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrashing mumkin." Biroq, depressiyaga chalinganlar odatda kuchning chuqur yetishmasligini boshdan kechiradilar va Jyudining qatʼiy yondashuvi asosan samarasiz boʻlib chiqdi, faqat Jeynni iloji boricha uning jamiyatidan qochishga undadi.

Oʻtmishga nazar tashlasak, Lyusining maslahati eng samarali boʻlib chiqdi. Vaqt oʻtishi bilan, Jeynning ahvoli asta-sekin yaxshilana boshladi, garchi uning tiklanishi uzoq davom etadigan jarayon boʻlsa ham, bu hissiy jarohatlarning bardavom tabiatining dalilidir.
